content:
FRP needs little maintenance, but the little it needs is regular: inspect twice a year, clean with mild detergent and water, check fasteners, and reseal any damage promptly. This routine extends FRP service life to 20-30 years and prevents small issues from becoming structural problems.

A Quick Answer

Unlike steel, FRP does not rust; unlike wood, it does not rot. As a fibre-reinforced plastic, its longevity is governed by the resin matrix and surface protection rather than by corrosion. Its maintenance load is low but real: a six-monthly inspection, periodic cleaning to remove dirt and chemical residue, fastener checks, and prompt repair of any surface damage. The two things that actually shorten FRP life are neglected damage (moisture ingress at cut edges) and aggressive environments (UV, chemicals) on unprotected surfaces. Address both with a simple routine and FRP products routinely deliver 20+ year service lives.

A Simple Maintenance Plan

Frequency Action
Monthly (heavy use) Visual check, remove debris
Every 6 months Inspection + cleaning + fastener check
Annually Full inspection, edge-seal check, UV coating review
After events Post-damage, chemical spill, or overload check

Adapt the frequency to the environment — a chemical plant needs more frequent attention than an indoor mezzanine. ASTM weathering standards provide the testing framework that predicts how outdoor FRP ages. Keep a simple log: date, findings, actions. Consistency beats intensity.

Regular Inspection Points

  • Surface: chalking, cracks, delamination, fiber bloom.
  • Edges: sealed? moisture staining? fiber exposure?
  • Connections: loose bolts, corrosion of hardware, adhesive joint condition.
  • Load points: wear, crushing, or deformation under high-load zones.
  • Anchors: base plates, grout, and concrete condition.

Most FRP problems start small and visible — delamination and edge damage are the two to catch early. Photograph findings and compare between inspections to track changes.

Cleaning FRP Correctly

Clean FRP with mild detergent and water, a soft brush or cloth, and gentle pressure washing (below ~100 bar, kept at a distance). Avoid harsh solvents, acids, and abrasives that can dull or soften the surface. For chemical plants, rinse promptly after spills — some chemicals attack the resin if left to dwell. The goal of cleaning is to prevent residue build-up that traps moisture and chemicals against the surface. Pressure washing with hot water helps remove oily residue; follow with a plain-water rinse.

UV & Weathering Care

Outdoor FRP slowly chalks (a cosmetic oxidation layer) as UV degrades the surface resin. Cleaning removes the chalk; for appearance-critical surfaces, a UV-protective coating (acrylic or polyurethane) refreshes the surface every few years. Structural performance is not significantly affected by chalking — the veil protects the glass — but heavy fiber bloom (fibers visible and fuzzy) indicates the veil is compromised and the surface should be recoated or sealed. Shade and orientation affect UV dose; south-facing (equator-facing) installations age fastest.

Fasteners & Connections

FRP itself does not corrode, but its stainless fasteners and steel anchors can — and a loose connection is a structural issue, not a cosmetic one. Check torque on bolted connections annually; re-torque any that have relaxed (FRP creeps slightly under sustained load, loosening bolts). Inspect adhesive-bonded joints for edge cracking or separation. Replace corroded hardware promptly with A2/A4 stainless. In wet environments, verify sealants at holes are intact.

Minor Repairs

Small problems are cheap to fix early. Scratches and minor surface damage: sand, clean, and seal with resin or gel coat. Loose fasteners: re-torque or replace. Small delamination at edges: inject epoxy, clamp, and reseal. Fiber bloom: clean and apply a UV coating. For structural damage — cracks through the section or impact breaks — treat as a structural repair per FRP repair guidance or replace the member. Never cover structural damage with paint and call it fixed.

How to Extend Service Life

Five habits double FRP service life: 
(1) inspect twice a year, 
(2) clean on a schedule, 
(3) reseal any cut or damaged edge immediately,
(4) check and re-torque fasteners
(5) protect from UV with coatings where appearance matters. FRP fails from neglect, not from age.

Also design for longevity at purchase: specify surface veils for outdoor use, fire-retardant resin where codes require, and stainless hardware from the start — ZEALL FRP products are manufactured with these choices so your maintenance load stays low for decades.

FAQ

Does FRP need maintenance?

Yes, but little: a six-monthly inspection, regular cleaning with mild detergent and water, fastener checks, and prompt repair of any damage. This routine extends service life to 20-30 years.

Can I pressure wash FRP?

Yes, gently — below about 100 bar, kept at a distance. High-pressure washing can damage the surface. Use mild detergent and finish with a plain-water rinse.

How do I remove chalk from FRP?

Chalking (the powdery white surface from UV oxidation) is removed by washing with mild detergent and water. For appearance-critical surfaces, apply a UV-protective coating afterwards.

How often should I inspect FRP structures?

At least twice a year in normal use; more often in chemical, marine, or heavy-load environments. Check surfaces, edges, connections, and anchors.

What shortens FRP service life most?

Neglected edge damage and moisture ingress, followed by harsh chemical exposure on unprotected surfaces. Prompt resealing and cleaning prevent both.
